002-habakkuk.title: Britain Tried to Build an Aircraft Carrier Out of Ice #shorts
lines: Britain once tried to build a warship out of ice.
The idea came from Geoffrey Pyke: freeze water with wood pulp. They called it pykrete.
It was stronger than ice, and melted far more slowly. The ship was planned at six hundred meters long.
On a lake in Canada, they built a scale model. It still weighed a thousand tons.
But the real ship needed enormous resources. By the end of nineteen forty-three, it was shelved.
The model slowly melted, and sank to the bottom of the lake.

003-bat-bomb.title: The US Strapped Firebombs to Bats. They Burned Their Own Base. #shorts
lines: America armed bats with fire bombs.
The idea came from a dentist, Lytle Adams, who wrote to President Roosevelt in nineteen forty-two.
Sleeping bats would be dropped over Japanese cities, and roost in the roofs. Each one with a tiny timed firebomb.
Then, in nineteen forty-three, armed bats escaped at an airfield in New Mexico.
They roosted in the buildings, and burned much of the base.
The Navy and the Marines kept testing. In nineteen forty-four, the project was dropped.
